cards.name: Gloom
cards.notes: Gloom from Cosmic Eclipse 3/236 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As an uncommon card, it is useful for collectors who want the sleepy theme to feel complete beyond only the expensive hits. The card is illustrated by sui, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. Its low market price makes it one of the easiest sleepy Pokemon cards to add to a binder without stretching a collection budget. It can help bridge older modern sets with newer illustration rares in a mixed-era sleepy Pokemon layout.
cards.whyItBelongs: Cozy nap in an open green pasture. Sui captures Gloom in peak peaceful drool mode under the warm afternoon sun.

cards.name: Tepig
cards.notes: Tepig from Cosmic Eclipse 31/236 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As a common card, it is useful for collectors who want the sleepy theme to feel complete beyond only the expensive hits. The card is illustrated by Mina Nakai, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. Its low market price makes it one of the easiest sleepy Pokemon cards to add to a binder without stretching a collection budget. It can help bridge older modern sets with newer illustration rares in a mixed-era sleepy Pokemon layout.
cards.whyItBelongs: Tepig has completely crashed on the bed, face-down against a pillow with its Poké Ball left nearby. Mina Nakai’s soft, rumpled bedding and wonderfully ungraceful sleeping pose make this feel less like a carefully planned nap and more like a tiny Fire-type who simply ran out of energy.

cards.name: Rockruff
cards.notes: Rockruff from Cosmic Eclipse 123/236 lounges on a pastel bed, looking just shy of waking.
cards.whyItBelongs: Rockruff has claimed a soft bed and is lounging with the relaxed, heavy-lidded look of a pup resisting wake-up time. The pastel bedroom scene makes this one of the collection's coziest indoor rests.

cards.name: Vileplume-GX
cards.notes: Vileplume-GX from Cosmic Eclipse 211/236 is included in this guide as a sleepy Pokemon card for collectors building a calm, cozy, or nap-themed binder. As a Rare Ultra, it is one of the showier entries in the sleepy Pokemon theme and can carry a page on its own. The card is illustrated by Kagemaru Himeno, which is useful context for collectors who like arranging pages by artist as well as by Pokemon. Its high market price puts it firmly in grail territory for a sleepy Pokemon collection, so it is best treated as a long-term chase card. It can help bridge older modern sets with newer illustration rares in a mixed-era sleepy Pokemon layout.
cards.whyItBelongs: Erika has dozed off against her Vileplume, and her longtime partner seems to have drifted off right alongside her. It’s especially fitting for a Gym Leader who has been caught snoozing in the games since Kanto: surrounded by flowers and leaning into one of her signature Pokémon, Erika has apparently found yet another place to fall asleep.

cards.name: Mega Lopunny & Jigglypuff-GX
cards.notes: Jigglypuff is awake while Lopunny rests with its eyes closed in a cozy embrace.
cards.whyItBelongs: Jigglypuff looks delighted to be awake, but Lopunny has already settled into a contented doze in its arms. Shibuzoh's warm, flower-filled illustration makes this Tag Team card feel like a gentle cuddle that turned into a nap.
